title: How to play on ESL Versus

posts.h:
1. Go to the official Brick-Force ESL page - http://www.esl.eu/eu/brick-force/

2. Click on the "Play VS." icon.




3. A flash window will pop-up, with a big list of games, chose Brick-Force.



4. In the right side of the window, you'll see the rules, our server (ESL Europe) with a number of players that are already playing or waiting for a match, a voice server where you can talk with other Brick-Force players, and the "Search for a match" button. Click on the "Search for a match" button.



5. Now, a new window will pop-up under the "Play VS." icon.



6. From now, we need to wait for the players to join the match so we can play, until that we can click on the "Open waiting chat" line to talk to the others.



7. When the match is ready to begin, all the players will be informed about that and a room will be made in-game, all the players must join that room to play.

I hope it's helpful and I also wanna see more players on ESL, high quality gaming is always fun!

title: A Guide to Getting Started on ESL VERSUS

posts.h:
Hey Brick-Forcers!

We’re proud to have joined forces with the Electronic Sports League (ESL) to bring competitive gaming to Brick-Force using their VERSUS platform. VERSUS is the new matchmaking system from the ESL, bridging the game between public gaming and the competitive ladders of the ESL making it easier to find people to play with than ever before.

Our integration with ESL VERSUS will included 4v4 Build and Destroy, 3v3 Capture the Flag, and 2v2 Team Deathmatch. Cash prizes and rewards are up for grabs if you are ready to step up to the challenge.

For those of you that have not used VERSUS for any of your other favorite titles in this past, I’ve put together this short step-by-step guide to matchmaking.

Firstly, please make sure you select the correct portal:

  • EU Players: http://www.esl.eu/eu/versus

Playing a Match


  1. Firstly you will need to register for an ESL account or login to ESL at the top right of the screen.

    Once you are logged in, either click the grey “Play VS” logo at the top of your screen, or the orange Play! Button on the VERSUS page.


    OR

  2. In the window that appears, all supported titles are listed alphabetically. You can either search for Brick-Force or scroll until you see it in the list.

  3. After selecting Brick-Force, you can select your region and see how many players are online using ESL VERSUS on the right. Clicking the Rules button will bring up a dialog box listing the rules for the selected game type.


  4. You will be then placed in the matchmaking queue. This displays how much time you have been waiting, how many other players are searching for a match, and the estimated time until a match is found. There is also a chat room for all players in the queue. Matchmaking will automatically search for similarly skilled opponents.

  5. Before a match is created, you must click the “I’m ready!” button. Failure to do so before the timer runs out will result in you being placed back into the matchmaking queue.


  6. After indicating that you are ready, you will be taken to the matchmaking screen where teams are split and Map Voting begins. Once voting completes, it’s time to start up Brick-Force on your PC and play the desired match. Don’t forget to make your Game Room password-protected and give the password to your team-mates and opponents.


  7. Once you have completed your match, you can return to the ESL Versus page to enter the results. Remember to be honest with your results! If there are any discrepancies between teams, the match will be reviewed for accuracy by the ESL admins. Cheating will be taken very seriously and could result in permanent disqualification from the ESL.

    Clicking “No result” will bring up a dropdown menu of various reasons for no match result. Clicking the running man icon next to a player’s name indicates that they left the match.


  8. After entering your match results, you can visit the Match Details page for an overview of the match which includes all other players’ result entries that you can check for accuracy.

    You can also check your team rankings on the Winter Season 2012 scoreboard to find out how you are doing. Good luck. We hope your team plays well and has a chance at winning some great prizes!
posts.t: A Guide to Getting Started on ESL VERSUS

posts.h:
Creating a Team


You can even search for matches on VERSUS as a party. On the bottom right of your screen will be the menu pictured. Clicking on Party will open this menu. Sharing the generated link with your friends will allow them to join your party. Now you will search for a match together and even have your own party chat, away from the rest of the players.


Taking party play one step further is creating a Team. Clicking Teams in the top right of the screen when you are logged in will bring you to your Team page. This page will display all Teams that you are a member of and allow for you to create a new Team.


Here you can fill in all the above fields to complete your Team’s profile. Once your Team is created, invite your friends to join and you can compete on ESL VERSUS together and climb the rankings as a Team.

I hope this tutorial helps you get started on ESL VERSUS. If you don’t quite get the hang of something, feel free to ask me or Zal and we’d be more than happy to help you

We wish you the best of luck with your games, soldiers.

Okay, ESL is nice, but competitive. It has some flaws which people could use to win a match. I feel since it's such a competitive environment people are encouraged to use these flaws in the system even more.

The first design flaw. Suicides in TDM. Most shooters penalize the player for killing himself. Some make it where if you kill yourself while receiving damage from another player the kill goes to them. Which is perfectly fair. And some shooters make you lose score from killing yourself. Which would also be fair in my opinion. It'd stop people from even accidently killing themselves. Brickforce on the other hand allows you to kill yourself easily to gain back armour and health, and possibly stop your enemy from scoring a point in the heat of battle as well. This is more so a problem with TDM in general on brickforce, but it can abused on ESL in order to stand a much better chance.

The second debatable flaw is with 2vs2 TDM again. Map selection for this game mode offers all of the same maps really. That is Close Quarters Combat. There really is no opportunity to use a sniper properly on Boeing 747, Death Camp, or Saraios. Well, there is opportunity, but not enough since the maps tends to favour being close more often than not. It would be nice if there was at least a more varied selection, rather than having to bring a light gun to every single map because all of them are close combat for the most part.

My main complaints come from Death Camp. The map seems nice and seems well balanced. It seems like a close quarters map mostly at first, like all the other maps. The real problem is just about anywhere you can rain death upon the entire map with your grenades. So this map is more like a Grenade map(ever played Nyan Cat on the US server? It's the exact same way. Everyone spams nades until they run out, then usually die to someone else's nade too). There just isn't enough roofing cover anywhere to protect yourself when someone feels like throwing 8 grenades across the map. Pair this with them having heart beat radar, and 5 star grenades (that can easily do 100+ at the near edge of their radius, and 240+ if they get it spot on) and you are pretty much going to rack in the kills on this map and be unbeatable if you constantly use grenade refills.

Not to mention the spawn on Death Camp is just so more camp-able than the other maps. You're enemies usually tend turning that cover against you. And you don't have any cover if they decide to use that tower in the center of the map. The tower is a death sentence if you continue to stay up there, but it still is like a double edged sword. And once they get one kill, they don't have to stick around and you just wasted a grenade trying to bomb an empty roof.

What I suggest is replacing Death Camp with another map. One that is still small of course and tends to favour close quarters combat, but it's not a grenade mosh pit like Death Camp. Dusty is a perfect example of a decently well balanced map. Their are plenty of choke points for someone to use grenades on. There are plenty of closed in areas for close combat, and even some wide open areas for snipers and grenading as well. Not to mention all the ways you can flank your opponent. The only problem with Dusty is blue debately at a disadvantage, and you can break the map and get up on the edges of it which is also unfair. Either way I still think Death Camp should be swapped out. It's just too unbalanced when it comes to grenades.

I agree. I also suggested awhile ago to use Marv's Nuketown. Everyone knows that map and it is very well rounded for all players.

On teh US I have a total of 8 grenades almost instantly that are super sexy. I played on EU where I only have 4 moderate nades. I played a match against EU players on death camp, and I had 16 uber grenades tossed into our spawn within seconds of the game starting lol.
